findings.title: Judgment requires steadiness
findings.claim: Faithful judgment requires epistemic and temperamental steadiness; access to revelation alone does not prevent an agitated preference from seeking ignorant judgment.
findings.mechanism: The focus judging occurrences meet 5:50's paired contrast of sought ignorance and agitation with goodness and settled certainty, changing the command from possession of the right source alone into a demand on the judge's knowing and disposition.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive that the revealed criterion still has to be handled by a stable, discerning person; the source does not mechanically produce a sound decision.
findings.containment: The ordinary command to judge by what Allah sent down remains primary. The packet leaves open whether al-jāhiliyyah is chiefly a historical-social designation rather than a cognitive and affective mechanism.

epistemic.reason: The exact adjacent contrast is supplied, while reading it back as formation of the judge's epistemic and affective condition is attributed.

branch_activations.carrier: The supplied 5:50 word-3 occurrence, attributed as actively seeking an inferior judgment.

findings.claim: The designation أهل الإنجيل can be heard as enacted affiliation: the community shows which normative household governs it through its judgments, while refusal marks a possible exit.
findings.mechanism: The focus affiliation and breach occurrences meet 5:51's chosen alliance, 5:54's reversal and obedience, and 5:56's party formation, changing the community label from a fixed demographic description into a relation enacted by what governs conduct.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive belonging as something displayed through allegiance and practice: judgment reveals which norm the community actually lets govern it.
findings.containment: The primary reading still names the Gospel community and commands it to judge by what Allah sent down. The packet leaves open whether 5:51-5:56 should be read back into أهل الإنجيل or as a separate social sequence; the affiliation relation is exploratory.

epistemic.reason: Exact supplied anchors support affiliation, reversal, obedience, and party formation, but their return into the focus noun is explicitly an attributed exploratory inference.

findings.title: The named source as sustaining Lord
findings.claim: The added 1:2 overlay makes the named source in 5:47 perceptible as the One praised as Rabb of all worlds, so the revealed criterion is heard as coming from the same sustaining Lord addressed in praise.
findings.mechanism: The focus proper-name occurrences of Allah meet the external 1:2 occurrences that place the same name within praise and immediately associate it with sustaining all worlds; this adds a source-and-sustenance relation beyond the native pericope's named sourcehood.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the sender of the Gospel criterion not only as its named origin but as the sustaining Lord to whom praise is directed.
findings.containment: This is an external overlay on the focus source name. It does not claim that the focus verse itself states Rabb or all worlds, and it does not import the remaining Fātiḥa as an implicit whole-surah reading.

epistemic.reason: The shared focus proper-name occurrence and exact external 1:2 surface occurrences provide a local contact, while the source-and-sustenance synthesis is an inferred overlay.

The packet supplies no separately named semantic-obligation or required-facet fields. Each HFT before/after reading, mechanism, reader inference, and activation role is preserved in the retained finding or its branch activations.

The external Fātiḥa members have lean context projections rather than full target morphology. The three retained overlays are therefore bounded as qualified or exploratory; the added 1:3 and 1:5 material was reviewed and supplied no distinct focus carrier-trigger change.
The lower-signal native connections to 5:52, 5:53, and 5:55 were reviewed as surrounding context and added no distinct focus change; they are not used to create a negative inventory.
